newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PSG LOOK FOR FIRST EVER VICTORY OVER JUVENTUS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PSG LOOK FOR FIRST EVER VICTORY OVER JUVENTUS.

text.p: Paris Saint-Germain will be looking to beat world club champions Juventus for the first time in seven meetings when the two sides clash in the first leg of the European Supercup at Parc des Princes on Wednesday.
In their previous clashes in European competition, the Italian side have won four times, twice in Paris in successive UEFA Cup visits in October 1989 and April 1993.
Juventus' victory over PSG on the away goals rule on their way to winning the European Cup Winners' Cup in 1984 saw them go on to lift the Super Cup for the first time.

PSG's Brazilian manager Ricardo and his assistant Joel Bats would both like to take revenge for the defeats at the Parc. The former defender was in PSG's 1993 side, while the ex-France keeper played in 1989.

A victory for Cup Winners' Cup holders PSG, the first French side to play for the Super Cup, would give them a tremendous boost ahead of their trip to Monaco on January 26 for a key first division championship match.
It would also put an off-colour Juventus, seeking their third major trophy in nine months, under pressure for the return leg in Turin.
Juventus' French midfielder Didier Deschamps believes the Super Cup could be the Italian's first trophy of an equally successful 1997.
"We have the potential to win everything: the Super Cup against PSG, the title and the European Cup," France captain Deschamps told the French sports daily L'Equipe.
To make a winning start Juventus will need to improve on the one department that Deschamps considers a weakness: finishing.
"In relation to the quantity of chances we create, we fail with too many," Deschamps said.
Juventus, furthermore, will be without their injured Croatian striker Alen Boksic.

PSG plan to launch their talented 17-year-old Nicolas Anelka into the fray from the start with a brief to roam freely across the whole front of the attack in support of French international striker Patrice Loko and try to open gaps in the defence.
Ricardo's compatriot Leonardo, still recovering from injury, is unlikely to make more than a brief sortie from the bench.
"I'm not 100 percent, I'm not confident when I have to shoot," the Brazil midfielder said.

Central defender Alain Roche is unfit with fellow French international Bruno N'Gotty, who should have recovered from a knee injury, dropping back from midfield into his favourite position at the back alongside Paul Le Guen.

Juventus will make a late decision on whether to field their Uruguayan defender Paolo Montero, who was joining them directly in Paris after playing for his country against Argentina in a World Cup qualifier in Montevideo on Sunday night.
Paris Saint-Germain - Bernard Lama; Jimmy Algerino, Bruno N'Gotty, Paul Le Guen, Didier Domi; Alain Fournier, Vincent Guerin, Rai, Jerome Leroy; Patrice Loko, Nicolas Anelka.

Juventus - Angelo Peruzzi; Moreno Torricelli, Ciro Ferrara, Paolo Montero, Gianluca Pessotto; Angelo Di Livio, Didier Deschamps, Vladimir Jugovic, Zinedine Zidane; Michele Padovano, Alessandro Del Piero.
